title: Frontend: Concurrency Limited Task Scheduler
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Concurrency Limited Task Scheduler. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({limit,commands}). Deterministic dispatcher commands enqueue{id}, complete{id}, cancel{id}. After each command start queued jobs up to capacity. Return {active,queued,completed,cancelled}; preserve insertion order. Completing unknown IDs does nothing. Cancellation removes a queued or active job and releases capacity. IDs are unique.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Keep a queue and active count.
alternativeApproaches: Add backpressure and fairness priorities without starving old tasks indefinitely.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Queue while busy; rejection releases slot; synchronous throw.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
